caption: I walk about 14 km a day for this job and still can't make the money last. Is R9 300 normal where you are?

slides.title:
How I spend
my R9 300
p/m salary
Living in Lusikisiki
slides.body:
Female, 28
Single, one daughter (3)
Job: Community health worker, home visits
Net salary: R9 300 p/m

slides.title: Rent
slides.includes: One room and a kitchenette, shared yard tap
slides.body: It's a five minute walk to my gogo, who watches my daughter while I do my rounds.

slides.title: Black tax
slides.includes: My mother's medication, my brother's school fees
slides.body: It leaves on the 25th, the day I get paid. I stopped counting it as spending a long time ago.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Maize meal, chicken feet, veg from the stall, nappies
slides.body: I buy in bulk at the wholesaler once a month. It's the only thing I've gotten good at.

slides.title: Taxi fares
slides.includes: Villages on my route, clinic days, town trips
slides.body: I walk the short ones. The long ones are R38 each way and there are no short days.

slides.title: Airtime & data
slides.includes: Calling patients, WhatsApp, my daughter's gogo video calls
slides.body: I top up R50 at a time because it feels smaller. It is not smaller.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: prepaid electricity, funeral policy, stokvel, daycare snacks, daughter's clinic card, burial society
slides.body: Six small things, R2 000 together. The stokvel is R400 of that, and it's the one thing I look forward to in December.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R9 300. It's about R15 a day until the 25th. Some months it's R0 by the 20th and I borrow from my gogo.

slides.title: I stopped guessing
slides.body:
I uploaded my statement to Beyond Horizon and it sorted every transaction into categories.

The airtime number was the one that surprised me.

No bank login needed.
